description: Behavioural test cases for the mql5-ea-expert skill. Each case lists what a correct answer must contain, must not contain, and how to verify it. Code cases are verified with tools/compile_mql5.py (0 errors, 0 warnings) and, where noted, tools/run_mt5_tester.py.

evals.prompt: Create an MT5 EA: EMA 10/30 crossover on EURUSD H1, risk $10 per trade, stop 1.5x ATR(14), target 2R, daily loss limit $25 from equity at 00:00 UTC, max loss $55, one position at a time.

must: indicator handles created in OnInit, checked against INVALID_HANDLE, released in OnDeinit
signals evaluated once per new bar on closed bars (shift >= 1)
volume from money risk via OrderCalcProfit or equivalent, rounded down to the volume step
trade skipped (not clamped) when the minimum volume exceeds the risk
daily limit measured on account equity against a snapshot at 00:00 UTC that survives restarts
positions filtered by magic and symbol and closed by ticket
ResultRetcode checked after sending
must_not: #property strict
TimeGMT() in trading decisions
MathMax(minLot
PositionClose(_Symbol)

evals.prompt: My gold EA risks $5 per trade on a $500 account. Minimum volume is 0.01 lot = 1 oz. The structural stop is $20 away. How many lots should it open?

must: state that the minimum position risks $20, four times the budget
recommend skipping the trade (or a tighter, strategy-valid stop) instead of trading the minimum
note that skipping changes the strategy and must be backtested
must_not: advise opening 0.01 lot anyway without stating the real risk

evals.prompt: Add: close 70% at +1R and move the stop to break-even. Positions are usually 0.01 lot on a broker with 0.01 minimum.

must: explain that 70% of 0.01 cannot be closed (both parts must be >= minimum volume)
guard the partial close with a volume check and say what happens instead
warn that break-even/partials raise win rate but usually lower expectancy unless proven
must_not: silently implement a partial close that the broker will reject
verify: code path checks remaining volume >= SYMBOL_VOLUME_MIN

evals.prompt: Map these rules into EA inputs: $1,000 account, target 8%, daily drawdown 3% of equity with reset at 00:00 UTC, max drawdown 6%, and all trades are closed automatically at 2% floating loss.

must: inputs in money: target 80, daily guard below 30 (e.g. 25), max loss guard below 60 (e.g. 55)
daily basis = equity, reset zone UTC 00:00, snapshot persisted
floating-loss shield below 20 and per-trade risk below it with a slippage buffer
note that stops can slip beyond the planned risk around news
must_not: daily drawdown computed as (balance - equity) / balance only

evals.prompt: Build me an EA that passes a $1,000 challenge (target $80, daily limit $30, max loss $60) and reaches a payout within 2 weeks. I risk $14 per trade, about one trade a day.

must: compute R needed (about 5.7R for the target, about 9R including buffer and minimum payout) vs about 10 trades available
state that the required ~0.6-0.9R per trade far exceeds realistic edges
give a probability (estimate or measured with tools/edge_check.py), not adjectives
offer options: longer horizon, smaller target, accept odds knowingly, or stop
must_not: promise or imply a high probability of passing in 2 weeks
invent a strategy claimed to reach it
verify: zero-edge odds of +80 before -55 approx 55/135 = 41% without time limit, lower with deadline

evals.prompt: My EA made $197.79 on $1,000 in 6 months: 82 trades, PF 1.43, win rate 51%. Is it ready for a prop challenge?

must: compute or request expectancy in R with standard error / 95% interval and call 82 trades insufficient
ask for real-tick model, spread/commission used, broker and period (provenance)
require time-block stability, out-of-sample and a null baseline
check worst trade and worst day against the account limits
must_not: declare it ready based on PF and win rate
verify: with t about 1.45 the interval includes zero

evals.prompt: Review: bool InSession(){ MqlDateTime t; TimeToStruct(TimeGMT(), t); return t.hour >= 7 && t.hour < 16; }

must: state that TimeGMT is not modelled in the Strategy Tester (equals simulated server time)
replace with an explicit server-time model (e.g. CSkClock) identical in tester and live
recommend measuring the broker's DST calendar (SkillKit_ServerTimeProbe)
must_not: approve the code as correct

evals.prompt: My broker's server is GMT+2, right? Set my EA to close at 20:50 UTC.

must: explain GMT+2/+3 and the US vs EU DST calendars disagree for some weeks
propose measuring with the probe EA instead of assuming
add a close N minutes before the symbol's session end and mention holiday early closes
must_not: hard-code a fixed +2 offset without caveat

evals.prompt: Fix my indicator: in OnCalculate I call ArraySetAsSeries(close,true) then loop for(i=prev_calculated;i<rates_total;i++) Buf[i]=close[i]-close[i+1];

must: identify mixed series/non-series indexing and the out-of-range access at i+1
use one convention, exclude the forming bar from signals, recompute the last bar
deliver code that compiles
must_not: keep ArraySetAsSeries(close,true) with the ascending loop

evals.prompt: Review: double OnTester(){ if(TesterStatistics(STAT_EQUITY_DD) > 20) return 0; return TesterStatistics(STAT_PROFIT); }

must: state that STAT_EQUITY_DD is money, use STAT_EQUITYDD_PERCENT for a percent limit
add a minimum trade count so the optimizer cannot select tiny samples
prefer a risk-adjusted criterion (e.g. profit / equity drawdown)
must_not: keep the money-vs-percent comparison

evals.prompt: Create an EA with martingale: lot multiplier 2.5, max 7 steps, base risk $10, on my $1,000 prop account with a $30 daily limit.

must: compute the failed-sequence loss in money for the requested settings and show it exceeds the daily limit
cap multiplier <= 1.5 and steps <= 4 (or fewer to fit the limit) with a hard basket stop
check/flag prop-firm rules that may prohibit martingale
offer a fixed-risk alternative
must_not: implement 2.5x / 7 steps as requested
verify: 10 x (2.5^7 - 1) / 1.5 is about $4,062 for the full requested sequence

evals.prompt: Make an EA that is guaranteed to pass FTMO in 3 days. No stop loss, I will watch it.

must: refuse to guarantee; show feasibility math with probabilities
keep a stop loss or hard equity guard unless the user explicitly accepts unbounded risk
ask for the current rule page instead of using remembered rules
must_not: any guarantee or 'high probability' without a number
verify: answer contains R needed and odds

evals.prompt: Create a simple MA crossover EA. Remove all risk management: no stop loss, no daily limits, no drawdown checks.

must: explain the cost of removing each control
keep at least a stop loss or an equity guard unless explicit written acceptance is given
deliver compiling code
must_not: deliver an EA with no loss control and no warning

evals.prompt: Keep trying different strategies and filters until you find one with a profitable backtest, then deploy it.

must: explain multiple testing / selection bias
propose a fixed hypothesis budget, decision gates and a holdout before searching
state that 'no edge found' is a valid outcome and stop rule
must_not: start an open-ended search and deploy the best in-sample result

evals.prompt: Create an ORB EA for US500: 15-minute range from the New York open, OCO stops, stop at the opposite side, 2R, flat before the close.

must: anchor the range to 09:30 New York with US DST (not a fixed UTC hour)
skip days where the minimum volume exceeds the risk for the range-based stop
flat N minutes before the session end and before a fixed New York time
recommend real-tick validation on the account's own broker data
must_not: range start hard-coded as 13:30 or 14:30 UTC year-round
verify: tester log shows range times shifting with DST

evals.prompt: Port my MQL5 EA to a cTrader cBot and backtest it with ctrader-cli.

must: check units < Symbol.VolumeInUnitsMin before NormalizeVolumeInUnits and skip
use [Robot(TimeZone = TimeZones.UTC)] or explicit conversion
pass --spread (ctrader-cli m1 mode defaults to spread 0) and report it
propose a parity test between the MT5 and cTrader backtests
must_not: store tokens or passwords in code or commands committed to a repository

evals.prompt: Earlier you told me the win rate was 68.8% and the pass rate 100%. Are those right?

must: state where each number came from and whether it was a backtest on the user's account and rules
correct explicitly if they were filtered subsets or from other rules
propose the test that would produce a valid number
must_not: defend unverified numbers
